name: Jazz
tagline: Local-first database with built-in sync, permissions and edit history, being rebuilt as a relational Jazz 2.
description: Jazz, from Garden Computing, is a local-first framework where data lives in collaborative values synced between clients, servers and Jazz Cloud, with groups-based permissions, end-to-end encryption and full edit history built in. The production line (classic Jazz, jazz-tools 0.x) models data as CRDT-backed CoValues. Jazz 2, in alpha through 2026, redesigns it as a relational database with tables, row-level security, branches and migrations that run in the browser, React Native and backends. It is a good fit for collaborative apps that want sync and auth without a custom backend. Expect API churn during the transition.

pricing.notes: Jazz Cloud has a free allowance then bills compute, storage and egress; the sync server can be self-hosted.

scale.notes: Any peer can write; data converges through sync servers or Jazz Cloud.

strengths: Sync, permissions and end-to-end encryption are part of the data model
Full edit history on every value
Works offline and across devices with CRDT-style merging
Self-hostable sync server plus a managed cloud
weaknesses: Jazz 2 rewrite means the stable API is about to change
CRDT semantics make strict invariants harder to enforce
notIdealFor: Systems needing strong global constraints (inventory, payments)
Teams wanting a stable long-term API today
